findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser row is missing
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then immediately dereferences tu.notification_level. Users who were never tracked in a topic (e.g. emailed via mailing-list mode, digest, or just lurkers) have no TopicUser row, so tu is nil and the request raises NoMethodError on nil instead of unsubscribing. Use TopicUser.change/get-or-create or handle nil before changing notification_level.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe via GET enables CSRF
findings.body: In app/controllers/topics_controller.rb TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification_level and saves on a GET route (config/routes.rb get t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe). GET requests have no CSRF token check, so any third-party image/link visited by a logged-in user can silently downgrade/mute their topic subscription. State changes must use POST/PUT/DELETE with CSRF protection or a signed single-use token.

findings.title: New unsubscribe_link interpolation breaks emails without unsubscribe_url
findings.body: In config/locales/server.en.yml unsubscribe_link now requires %{unsubscribe_url}, and lib/email/message_builder.rb renders it unconditionally in body (line 90) and html_part (line 67) whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. Any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without passing unsubscribe_url (only UserNotifications#send_notification_email was updated) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send the email. Provide a default/fallback or keep the old text when unsubscribe_url is absent.

findings.title: SPA unsubscribe page never calls server unsubscribe action
findings.body: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6 the model hook calls PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id), which hits the normal topic show endpoint, not TopicsController#unsubscribe. A user navigating client-side to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe therefore never executes the server-side notification_level downgrade; the mutation only happens on full-page Rails render. Either have the route call the unsubscribe endpoint or move the mutation to an explicit user action.
